title: Real-Time Deadlines Reveal Fragile Temporal Adaptation in LLM Strategic Dialogues
abstract: arXiv:2601.13206v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text token-by-token in discrete time, yet real-world communication, from therapy sessions to business negotiations, critically depends on continuous time constraints. We use simulated negotiations between paired agents under strict deadlines to study adaptation to real-time pressure. Agents either receive only the initial deadline or explicit remaining-time updates at each turn. Remaining-time feedback raises deal closure from 4% to 32% for GPT-5.1-chat-latest and increases offer acceptance more than sixfold. The same model achieves near-perfect closure under turn-based limits, showing that poor wall-clock performance is not simply due to insufficient negotiation competence. translated_title: 实时截止期限揭示大语言模型策略对话中脆弱的时间适应能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）以离散时间方式逐token生成文本，然而现实世界的沟通——从心理治疗到商业谈判——都严重依赖于连续的时间约束。我们使用配对智能体在严格截止期限下的模拟谈判来研究对实时压力的适应能力。智能体要么只接收初始截止期限，要么在每一轮对话中接收明确的剩余时间更新。剩余时间反馈使GPT-5.1-chat-latest的成交率从4%提升至32%，并使报价接受率提高六倍以上。同一模型在基于轮次的限制下几乎能达到完美的成交率，这表明糟糕的现实时钟表现并非仅仅源于谈判能力不足。在额外的接口条件下，定性的紧迫性提示可以胜过数字倒计时，重复的截止期限提醒并不能稳定地复现其收益，而定向的时间追踪可能有益也可能有害。
tldr: 该研究通过实时截止期限下的模拟谈判揭示，大语言模型的时间适应能力十分脆弱——实时压力使GPT-5.1的谈判成交率骤降至4%，而提供剩余时间反馈可将其恢复至32%，表明其瓶颈在于时间适应机制而非谈判能力本身。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that LLMs exhibit fragile temporal adaptation under real-time deadlines—deal closure collapses to 4% under time pressure yet recovers to 32% with remaining-time feedback—demonstrating that the bottleneck lies in temporal adaptation rather than negotiation competence.
